audit.whatIsWrong: Defiant Dance (W) is never mentioned anywhere in either layer, in a matchup Zac wins 55.83% of the time over 206 games.
audit.why: Riot's text: "She takes reduced physical damage during the charge." Physical only. Zac's Unstable Matter is explicitly "a percentage of their maximum health as magic damage", so Irelia's one defensive button in a duel mitigates the wrong damage type against him. This is the most likely single explanation for the win rate and it is completely absent from the entry.
audit.corrected: Defiant Dance reduces physical damage only; Unstable Matter is magic, so her duel button reads the wrong damage type.

audit.whatIsWrong: early calls Stretching Strikes "your short-range Q" against Irelia, and spikes[0] has Bladesurge letting her "dance in and out of your Stretching Strikes".
audit.why: Stretching Strikes is 800 range; Bladesurge is 600. Zac out-ranges her dash by 200 units, which reverses who is being kited. Both lines teach the opposite of what the numbers say.
audit.corrected: Your Q reaches 800; her Bladesurge covers 600.

audit.whatIsWrong: Irelia's passive is called "shred" twice — "her passive shred beat your short-range Q" and "her passive stacks shred your blobs".
audit.why: Ionian Fervor is stacking bonus Attack Speed, plus bonus damage on hit at maximum stacks. There is no resistance reduction anywhere in the kit. "Shred" implies armour reduction and would push a Zac player away from resistances that in fact still work.
audit.corrected: Stacking attack speed, then bonus on-hit damage at max stacks — no resistance reduction.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three separate places claim Vanguard's Edge cancels Zac's engage: mid ("her R can cancel your Slingshot"), spikes[1] ("can cancel your Slingshot mid-flight") and wants.foe[2] ("wall to cancel your Slingshot").
audit.why: Riot's text for Vanguard's Edge describes blades that damage and Mark, then "form a wall that will damage and slow enemies that walk through it". Damage, a Mark and a slow — no interrupt and no displacement is described anywhere. Teaching a Zac player to refuse every engage into an available ultimate costs him the windows this matchup is won in. Rewritten to state what the wall does do: block a retreat and hand her Marked targets to reset Bladesurge on.
audit.corrected: Vanguard's Edge Marks what it hits and leaves a wall that damages and slows — a retreat-blocker and a reset engine.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere; breakdown.cooldowns reads "matchup-defining — Her engage CC. E-knock/dodge it."
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16s at rank 1 against Elastic Slingshot's 21s, so Zac is the one who cannot afford to go first. And Flawless Duet is two blades that must converge — sidestepping one half is the counterplay, which "dodge it" does not convey.
audit.corrected: Flawless Duet 16s at rank 1 vs your Slingshot 21s — make her spend the stun first. Two blades must converge; sidestep one.

audit.whatIsWrong: The content chart gives Irelia 6 of 7 stages and Zac 0 while Zac wins 55.83% over 206 games — the largest sample in this slice. The full layer separately reads Irelia / Skill / Zac / Zac / Irelia / Zac / Zac, so the two layers also disagree with each other.
audit.why: The full layer's split is both consistent with the win rate and consistent with the kit facts above: Irelia genuinely owns level 1 (Bladesurge resets before Zac has a second ability) and level 6 (Vanguard's Edge), while the middle and post-item stages belong to Zac because his range advantage and magic-damage W both bypass what her kit is built to answer. Aligning the content chart to the full layer fixes the contradiction and the cross-layer inconsistency in one move.
audit.corrected: Irelia / Skill / Zac / Zac / Irelia / Zac / Zac.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal is not mentioned in the content layer.
audit.why: Bladesurge heals Irelia on every cast, and it refunds its cooldown off Marked or dying targets, so in a reset chain the healing compounds rather than being a one-off. _missing-interactions.json flags this matchup for needs-antiheal on exactly that ability.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds — Bladesurge heals her on every reset in the chain.

notes:
The Vanguard's Edge "cancels your Slingshot" claim is the one I would most like a second pair of eyes on. I rated it Medium rather than High because I am arguing from absence — Riot's ability text describes damage, a Mark and a slow, and describes no interrupt — rather than from a positive source saying it cannot interrupt. I did not write any line asserting that it cannot; the replacement text only states what the wall does. If the League Wiki confirms the wall has no interrupt component, this can be raised to High.

phases[i].side, diff and diffRating are all shorter than the 12-character minimum the applier requires for a full-layer `before`, so the full layer keeps diff "TRICKY" / 7.5/10 even though 55.83% over 206 games reads closer to favoured. Only the content win[] chart could be corrected here.

WKM_LINES to verify (champion-level, irelia line 1): "Four stacks = her win button". Ionian Fervor stacks are not numbered in Riot ability text, so the count needs a wiki source. Line 2, "Every minion is a dash", overstates it slightly — Bladesurge refunds only off Marked targets or minions that die to it.
